Text describes Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE). Facts:

- The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE) is an Act of the Parliament of India.
- Enacted on 4 August 2009.
- Describes modalities of importance of free and compulsory education for children between age 6 to 14 years in India under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.
- India became one of 135 countries to make education a fundamental right of every child when the act came into force on 1 April 2010.
- Title of the RTE Act incorporates the words "free" and "compulsory".
- Free education means that no child, other than a child admitted by parents to a school not supported by the appropriate Government, shall be liable to pay any fee/charges/expenses which may prevent him/her from pursuing and completing elementary education.
- Compulsory education casts an obligation on the appropriate Government and local authorities to provide and ensure admission, attendance and completion of elementary education by all children in the 6-14 age group.
- India has moved forward to a rights based framework that casts a legal obligation on the Central and State Governments to implement this fundamental child right as enshrined in Article 21A, in accordance with provisions of the RTE Act.
